item.title: How a 311 complaint can stop a foodborne illness outbreak
item.description:
Foodborne illness affects thousands of New Yorkers every year. A foodborne illness outbreak is when two or more people get sick from consuming food or drink from the same establishment, prompting the New York City Health Department to investigate and try to prevent further illness.

Let’s look at a real foodborne illness outbreak investigation that took place in NYC:

Two people dined together at a restaurant. Three days later, both diners became very sick. One went to the emergency room and tested positive for Campylobacter, a bacterium that lives in raw or undercooked animal products and can cause gastrointestinal (stomach) illness. Eight days after the dinner, the diner who visited the emergency room called 311 to report both illnesses. In addition to seeing a doctor, you should call 311 if you think you got sick after eating food from a NYC restaurant.

item.title: Tracking food poisoning outbreaks in NYC restaurants—what makes us sick and why
item.description:
Each year, the NYC Health Department receives thousands of complaints of foodborne illness, commonly called “food poisoning.” When two or more people get sick after consuming a common food or drink, we investigate a potential foodborne illness outbreak.

We start by reviewing 311 complaints about food poisoning from eating and drinking establishments. These include restaurants, food carts and trucks, bakeries, bars, cafeterias, catering services, correctional facilities, hospitals, delis, soup kitchens, and summer camps.

item.title: What hot weather means for food safety
item.description:
New Yorkers eat out more than a billion times a year. To help keep diners safe, the Health Department educates restaurant operators about food safety practices and inspects all 27,000 city restaurants at least once a year. Over 90 percent of NYC restaurants have “A” grades in the window, showing excellent compliance with food safety requirements.

However, warmer weather creates special challenges keeping food safe. We dug into the data to find out how hot weather affects food safety.
